about: The file after each act of fixed sequences that the model plays, World.step and World.act of model/crdt_model.py of spikes/storage/probes/store-as-a-whole on spikes/storage-survival under the FLAGS of probe/bridge.py, the store as decided, written out as entries by store.py's Encoder as the family's runs write them, and read by read.py with its history rule on; made by vectors.py beside the probe and never from this side. Each sequence starts from the store the model's World starts with, given as start: the authority a0, the profile name pf, the admission of the client c0 under a0 with the profile pf alone, a version of the row of each of the profiles pf and pg at the root granting read, and a summary entry of height 1, each under the key label K; the two copies of the second and of the third sequence start as the same file. A pairing admits its client with the profiles pf and pg, and a renewal with the profiles of the admission renewed. The first sequence raises the model's maxclients to 4, as growth.py raises it, so that three pairings fit beside c0. The first Create of the sequence asked for, on a database with no store, is not played. On a file with no store the model's Create writes its authority under a new key label, K and a number, while its pairing writes every admission under the label K whatever key the file holds; played from emptied files, every admission after that Create was under a key the file does not hold, passed over by read.py, and the revocation did not apply. The Create after Delete is played: it takes the key the retirement holds. Each step names the command, the model's act, the copy whose file follows, whether the act applied, the store keys of the records present, every record present and every deletion record in the file by identifier, kind, subject and number, the deletion records the step added, each summary entry present with its identifier, its height, the count of its after and its items, read.py's answer as the meanings file gives it, and the file itself. Synchronize is the model's kp_sync merge of a copy into the other, which writes the copy merged into alone: copy 1 into copy 0 in the second sequence, and in the third copy 1 into copy 0 and then copy 0 into copy 1. The third sequence revokes the client c0 in copy 0 and renews its certificate in copy 1, the model's renewcert, which admits the certificate c0.1 under the client key c0 beside the admission of c0, before the copies are synchronized. The records hold v, the model's short names (a0, c1), nonces derived from the model's elements and store keys derived from its labels, so the product holds them by shape and by answer. What the model writes otherwise than STORE.md fixes: no version record at Create and no item format in any summary entry (650, 611); an authority holding id and storeKey alone (614); an admission without der, subject and admitted (615), and a renewal's without from as well (648); a revocation that also holds certificate (615); and a retirement for keeping an authority that does not hold the store key (614). The fourth sequence plays the model's padd and prem, the commands Add and Remove of a profile name, on two copies that start as the same file: pf removed in copy 0 and added again there, naming that removal; pf removed in copy 1; pg added in each copy; a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and then of copy 0 into copy 1; pf added again in copy 0, naming both removals; and the two Synchronize again in the same order. Once the copies meet, pf is off the list in both and pg on it by two additions, and once pf is added again and synchronized, it is on the list in both, and both copies hold the same file. The model's pairing writes no addition for a name it approves, which STORE.md 627 has a pairing write: no pairing here puts pg on the list. Every sequence plays with the store's rows switched on, the identifier of a row's version in the form split of store.py, in the form by what arrived (the form seen of S34-DESIGN.md) with a removed row taken off for real, as bridge.dep('seen', 'off') sets them, and the texts and objects of the records file: the start holds a version of the row of each profile at the root, row:R. Each sequence holds the profiles it plays with as profiles, the model's nodes by identifier as nodes and the tree as tree. The model's node N is bb repeated 16 times, directly under the root, aa repeated 16 times; where a sequence has three levels, the model's group G, dd repeated 16 times, is directly under the root and N under G. A sequence plays with the profiles pf and pg and the model's letters read and write, written R and U, but O6, O7, L8, L9 and L10, which play with the profiles pf, pg, ph and pi and the full mask, as they were measured; the model's letters are then those of CRUSDLAP in lower case, written in capitals. Every answer adds rules, read.py's answer about rules at each node as the meanings file gives it, capabilities among it. Every Synchronize adds beyond: what the copy merged into gives at each node beyond both copies just before the merge, letters neither copy gave and capabilities neither copy gave, as store_runs.py's part_dep holds a merge to both copies; only a node with something beyond is there. A version present or named by a deletion record adds its object, and for a row its subject and its number are those its identifier holds, as the records file gives them. The sequences whose names begin with rules and a comma are those of measured-rules-per-profile sections 4, 5 and 7 that run over two copies, each named by its label there, 5 for the two copies of section 5: A1 to A7, 5, D1 to D3, and W1 to W8. Each plays a base in copy 0, a Synchronize into copy 1, the acts of each copy apart, and then a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and of copy 0 into copy 1. Where the report sets several rows in a single act, each row is an act of its own, in the order of the profiles' names; an act of the report that changes no row is not played, as the root grants read from the start; and D1 to D3 remove a version in the form again, which STORE.md 617 fixes. The commands: Set row is the model's row act with letters, an empty rule where it holds none; Remove row its row act with off, which writes nothing where no row of the profile stands but versions that take the rule off, writes off:deny where the copy reads the node's switch as refusing, and otherwise writes anew each version of the switch that holds other letters for the profile than arrive, then takes the rule off with the letters that arrive; Set switch its switch act with deny, or with inherit, which records for each profile the letters that arrive, writes nothing where no version of the switch stands or a single version inherits already, and writes anew each version at the node that takes a rule off and holds other letters than arrive for its profile, off:deny among them; Set rows its rule act with a table, a version for each row the table names at the node, in a single write; Settle limit its lift act, the press that settles: each version at the node that lets the profile through and holds other letters than arrive written anew, a version of the switch with that profile's letters changed and every other profile's kept; Remove version its drop act, which writes again each version left, naming the version removed, the version left and everything each of them names. After every act at a node with nodes below, the write above: each node below, the nearer first, whose switch does not refuse and whose row does not answer by itself, where what arrives differs before and after the act and every version there that lets the profile through held everything that arrived before it, has those versions written anew, each by itself, with what arrives after, naming the version it renews and everything that version names; a version that was cutting already, or off:deny, leaves every version of its node for that profile as it is. An act's letters are the model's, and its node is the model's name. A step whose act writes nothing has played false and the copy's file as it stood: the second removal in W6. No Synchronize of A1 to W8 gives anything beyond both copies. At the end of W8 N gives pf R, what the first copy gave, where the store as decided gave R and U; W3 ends with nothing for pf; and W6 ends with pf given R and U, wider than the store as decided by design: the switch turned off in the second copy renews off:deny with what arrives (H9), as measured-rules-across-levels section 4 has it. Left out are the sequences of section 5 over three copies, D4 and D5, and W9, which writes a node's rule whole. The sequences whose names begin with form and a comma: O6 and O7 of measured-rules-owed-forms (merges4) and L8, L9 and L10 of its levels, each a base in copy 0, a Synchronize into copy 1, the acts of each copy apart, and a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and of copy 0 into copy 1, as measured-rules-across-levels section 4 played them; no Synchronize of them gives anything beyond both copies, O6 and O7 end with pf given A alone at N, a switch with no verb and so no capability, L8 with RL at G and at N, L9 with RL at N, and L10 with nothing for pf at N. H1, H3, H4, H9 and H10 of S34-DESIGN.md section 5, each as probe/s34.py plays it under the form: H1 then the press that settles in the copy that took the merge, and a Synchronize back; H10 with the root's row of pf first set to no letter, so that nothing arrives for pf, as the design states it, and pf ends with nothing at N. H4 is the residual history of the form: its last Synchronize gives pf R at N beyond both copies, within what the version at N recorded when its rule was taken off. R1a is the second residual history: G grants pf R and N holds an empty rule, the first copy takes the rule off N and the second takes it off G, both ways, and the root widened in the first copy reaches N, which ends with R and U, though no Synchronize gives anything beyond both copies. The sequence the write above names: a widening of the root in copy 1 renews G, where N still holds its empty rule; once both ways, N's version, taken off in copy 0 seeing R, cuts what G lets through to R; a narrowing of the root to R in copy 0 renews G and leaves N, which was cutting; and a widening again renews G and N, so that N, cut no longer by the time of that widening, follows it. What the model cannot express: it holds a switch under an object of its own name, sw: and the node, which store.py writes as switch: and the node's identifier; and its acts compose a version at the write, with no buffer: an act reads the copy's file as it stands when the act is played and writes at once, where STORE.md 629 has a rule set in a node's dialog written at the dialog's OK, naming what the tab showed at the press. So no vector holds a write at a dialog's OK that names only the versions the tab showed, nor a version that reached the database under an open dialog and is left by the write above; and the only write of several rows is the rule act, which sets the rows of a table at a single node, so no write here sets a row and the switch together. Every sequence here is played and read with the refinement of measured-lost-settled (crdt_model.JUDGE and read.JUDGE lost), which plays and reads every other sequence as it was. The sequences whose names begin with lost and a comma are its sequences, played with the tag of every name under the key of the model's label K as the model's acts see it (crdt_model.TAG_OF), so that what an act names is what read.py reads: p is q00331 and q q00534, whose tags meet at c699, z is q184933, whose tag is 0000, and r is pf. F1 is the sequence the measured reading is fail-open in, E1 to E3 ordinary edits of a name whose tag meets another's, L1 to L4 a loss at their place and each order of settling it, T1 to T3 the sequence of the product's test of two names whose tags meet, its order of settling turned and its copies exchanged, Z1 and Z2 a name whose tag is 0 beside a version of the object rule: and N with no slash, which is no node's rule, and W1 a lost version of the switch. In T1 to T3 the profiles pf and pg alone hold rows at the root, and p and q hold none. The further commands: Add name is the model's padd, a write that touches no rule; Settle row its settle act, a row that refuses for a lost version set to the letters its standing versions all grant; Lose version its lose act, a deletion record of a version of the object whose content no file holds; Delete by hand its del act, an entry of the store deleted for good with a deletion record or with none; and Set object with no slash its plain act. A version names in after the versions of its own object it replaces and what those name in after, and in lost the lost versions its row or switch shows at the write and what the versions it replaces name in lost. No Synchronize of these gives anything beyond both copies. The sequences whose names begin with answers and a comma are A1 to A14 of measured-renewal-answers, the standing answers to a renewal, played by the model with its answers on (crdt_model.ANSWERS) and read by read.py with its reading of answers on: each sequence's acts, then a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and of copy 0 into copy 1, then the acts that follow in copy 0. Every certificate and client key is written as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, the SHA-256 of kpg-store-as-a-whole/certificate/ and the model's name, a client's key that of its first certificate, and clients gives the key of c0 and of c1. An answer is a version of renew: and the client key, its text refuse:forever, refuse:until: and a moment, or ask, as in the records file; clock gives the three moments of the clock, and every step gives the clock of the copy whose file follows and its answer as renewals, as the meanings file gives it, and every Synchronize adds renewalsBeyond, each client whose answer after the merge is below both copies' just before it, of which there is none. The further commands: Refuse forever and Refuse until a date are the model's renew act with forever and with a moment, given only where the copy's reading asks at its clock, for a client admitted there; Allow renewal its renew act with ask, pressed only where the copy's reading refuses at its clock, naming in after the standing versions it was shown that still stand and in lost the lost versions it was shown, writing nothing where it names nothing; Show answer its see act, a dialog that shows the answer, whose shown versions the next answer of that copy about that client names, and no other; Set clock its clock act; Renew its renewcert act, refused where the copy's reading refuses at its clock; Pair and Revoke as before; Delete by hand, Seal again and Lose version as before; and Write text out of form its unreadable act, somebody holding the store key writing an answer whose text is refuse:until:2026-12-15 and a summary entry. The sequences whose names begin with seal and a comma are R1 to R21 of measured-seal, Seal again, played by the model with its answers and Seal again on (crdt_model.ANSWERS and SEAL) and read by read.py with its readings of answers and of what a stopped store lost on: each sequence's acts, then a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and of copy 0 into copy 1, then the acts that follow in copy 0. R3s, a lost version of the switch, is played with rows alone, and the rule of N is played on pf's row: Set rows with none empties every row at N. Every step adds damaged, each entry of the copy edited past the history limit, written with its content followed by a space and no history, and losses, read.py's listing as the meanings file gives it. The further commands: Show seal is the model's sealsee, the seal's dialog, applying only on a stopped store; Seal again its reseal: for each object a lost version makes refuse, a version granting nothing, naming in after the versions of the object in force and what they name there and in lost what was lost and what those name there; then a summary entry over everything that passes and is in force, every entry that is damage deleted with a deletion record, and every summary entry present, told of or damaged named in its after; refused where it would leave no entry holding the store key. Seal again with an act is its reseal+: the seal and the act in a single write with one summary entry, the act composed over the sealed store. Edit past the limit is its edit; Delete, Create and Recreate the commands on the authority, Create refused on a stopped store while a store key stands; Add name and Remove name its padd and prem; Merge by KeePassXC its xc merge. The sequence that holds accepted is the class of STORE.md 639 row 5, which the sequence ends in: the copy merged into admits the client whose revocation was lost with no deletion record before the seal, and a test holds it as accepted, never as decided. A7 of the answers is played past the seal already above, and with Seal again on it gives the same. The sequences whose names begin with starts and a comma are T1 to T16 of measured-started-again, a store started again, played by the model with its answers, Seal again and the keys of STORE.md 649 on (crdt_model.ANSWERS, SEAL and STARTS) and read by read.py with the same readings on: each sequence's acts, then a Synchronize of copy 1 into copy 0 and of copy 0 into copy 1, then the acts that follow in copy 0. Every step adds keysRead, the keys read.py finds, that stand and that it sets aside, each by the model's label, and keys gives the store key of each label. Start again is the model's restart: a new key, an authority holding it, under each key found a stop naming the new key that no summary entry restates, under the new key a keep record naming each key found and, in after, every keep record read and every stop, a version record of format 1 and a summary entry of height 1 restating them; it deletes nothing. Seal again over a store a start stopped writes a keep record under its key naming the key the stop names and the stop in after. Edit past the limit is the model's edit, which the files of these sequences write as the content followed by a space with no history; Raise the format is its newer, a version record of format 2 under the store key. The sequences whose names begin with restates and a comma are those of measured-seal-restates: R5 to R7 of measured-seal and F5 to F7r, a revocation, a retirement or a removal of a name that a deletion record alone tells of once its record and the summary entry are deleted, played by the model with its answers and Seal again on and the summary entry restating such a decision in the form proposed (crdt_model.SEAL_RESTATES ids), and read by read.py: each sequence's acts, every deletion record of copy 0 cleared where the name has deletion records cleared, then the merge the name gives into the copy it names, then the acts that follow in that copy. In F5 to F7r copy 1 is the copy from before the decision; in R5 to R7 it was synchronized after it. Where the seal finds a decision that a deletion record under the store key tells of and whose subject no record or item of the file names, its summary entry restates it by an item holding the identifier of that deletion record and the kind, revoked, retired or removed, and no subject; every summary entry after it carries the item while nothing names the subject, and restates the decision by its subject once something does. Such an item restates the record whose identifier it holds, and tells its decision of every subject the file names whose keyed hash under the key is the one the identifier holds. Clear deletion records removes every deletion record of the copy, as Database Maintenance does.
